dedupe_keys.name: shear modulus reduction and material damping ratio for microbially induced carbonate precipitated sands

description: Shear Modulus Reduction and Material Damping Ratio for Microbially Induced Carbonate Precipitated Sands is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Brina Montoya, North Carolina State University (ncsu.edu). Microbially Induced Carbonate Precipitation (MICP) is a bio-mediated ground improvement technique gaining attention in geotechnical engineering for enhancing soil stiffness and mitigating liquefaction. One critical factor in predicting seismic responses of MICP-treated sites is the characterization of strain-dependent dynamic behavior of the treated soils, including shear modulus reduction and damping ratio (MRD) curves. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Microbially Induced Carbonate Precipitation, MICP, shear modulus, damping ratio, dynamic properties, geotechnical engineering. Published 2026-08-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
